headline.text: The FDA colchicine label reports potentially fatal toxicity with protease inhibitors in patients with renal or hepatic impairment.

reported.text: The FDA warning covers atazanavir as a protease inhibitor and concerns patients with renal or hepatic impairment.
A spontaneous-report analysis also found a rhabdomyolysis or myopathy reporting signal for this specific pair.

claims.text: The FDA colchicine label reports life-threatening and fatal toxicity with protease inhibitors, including atazanavir's class, in patients with renal or hepatic impairment.
claims.quote:
Patients with renal or hepatic impairment should not be given colchicine tablets in conjunction with P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (this includes all protease inhibitors except fosamprenavir).
In these patients, life-threatening and fatal colchicine toxicity has been reported with colchicine taken in therapeutic doses.
claims.judgeRationale: The colchicine contraindication covers all protease inhibitors except fosamprenavir in renal or hepatic impairment and reports life-threatening and fatal toxicity; atazanavir is a protease inhibitor.

claims.text: A spontaneous-report analysis found a rhabdomyolysis or myopathy reporting signal for colchicine plus atazanavir, with reporting odds ratio 35.4.
claims.quote: The strongest ROR signal was for colchicine + atazanavir and rhabdomyolysis/myopathy (ROR = 35.4, 95% CI: 12.8-97.6)
claims.judgeRationale: The FAERS disproportionality abstract reports the strongest ROR signal for colchicine plus atazanavir and rhabdomyolysis/myopathy (ROR 35.4), and the claim frames it as a reporting signal.

pharmacistQuestions.text: The evidence here is limited. Is there anything about my health that makes this interaction more or less relevant?
Do any of my other medicines contain Atazanavir or Colchicine, or work the same way?
